Text file streaming11DPython treats content in a document as continuous character streams. When a document is opened, the system generates a hidden pointer to indicate the position being read at the moment, i.e. point to the first character.

Text file streaming12DIn text files, there are some special characters for controlling the formats of printing and display. Usually such characters are not shown in the document editor, but they are still stored in the text files:Line Feed (LF) character “\n” is stored at the end of every line;End Of File (EOF) character “EOF” is stored at the end of the text file.

Text file streaming13DIn Python, the read() function is used to read a document until it detects the EOF; while the readline() function is used to read a document until it detects a \n or reaches the end of the file. Take the following Python program as an example:
Text file streaming14D1. When the document is opened, the hidden pointer points to the first character.
Text file streaming15D2. The readline() function in the second line starts reading the document until the hidden pointer moves to the character after the \n character.

Text file streaming16D3. The readline() function in the third line starts reading the document from the position where the hidden pointer last stopped, until the hidden pointer moves to the character after the \n character.

Text file streaming17D4. The readline() function in the fourth line starts reading the document from the position where the hidden pointer last stopped. Since no \n is detected by the time the function reached the end of file, the function stops reading.
Text file streaming18D5. The hidden pointer reaches the end of file character. The readline() function in the fifth line returns an empty string.

Checking whether a text file exists8BIf the file to be opened does not exist, a run-time error occurs in the program. To avoid this, we should check whether a file exists before trying to open it. We can import the "os" library and use the path.exists() function to check whether the file or the path exists.
Checking whether a text file exists9BThis function returns a Boolean value: it returns True if the file exists; otherwise it returns False.
